answer: A falcon‑style reputation ledger timestamps each agent’s delta‑scaled contributions and links them to a cryptographic ripple of attestations from randomly chosen validators. When a new identity appears, it must supply a chain of signed attestations that match the current ripple pattern; mismatches trigger an automatic honeypot query that forces the claimant to answer a provably unique challenge. Generating enough valid attestations to spoof the ledger costs O(n²) computational work and a proportional stake, making large‑scale Sybil attacks economically infeasible.
